ru.B: Об этом нам нужно сказать очень многое, и это трудно объяснить, потому что вы стали вялыми слушателями.
ru.R: Нам нужно многое сказать об этом, но вам это трудно объяснить, потому что вы стали ленивы слушать.

uk.L: Про це в нас велике слово, і важко його пояснити, бо ви стали лінивими на слух.
uk.B: Про це нам треба сказати багато, і це важко пояснити, бо ви стали неуважними слухачами.
uk.R: Ми маємо багато що сказати про це, але вам важко це пояснити, бо ви полінувалися слухати.

ja.L: このことについて、わたしたちの話は多く、説明して言うのは難しいのです。あなたがたが、耳が鈍くなってしまっているからです。
ja.B: このことについては、話すべきことがたくさんありますが、言葉で説明するのは難しいのです。あなたがたが、聞くことに鈍くなっているからです。
ja.R: このことについては、話したいことがたくさんあります。けれども、みなさんに説明するのは難しいのです。みなさんは、話を聞くのがおっくうになってしまっているからです。

decisions.choice: concerning this: the subject of Christ's priesthood like Melchizedek's
decisions.reason: οὗ can be "which" (a subject) or "whom" (a person). Either way the topic is the one just named, a high priest of the order of Melchizedek, which the author takes up in chapter 7 after this warning.

decisions.choice: we: the author speaking of himself and his teaching
alternatives: the author and the readers together
decisions.reason: Here "we" stands over against "you" (the readers), so it is the author's own voice, as again in 6:9 and 6:11. Elsewhere in Hebrews "we" usually includes the readers (2:1, 4:14).

decisions.choice: you have become sluggish: dull and slow to take in teaching, as they were not at first
decisions.reason: νωθροὶ means slow, dull, lazy. "You have become" implies that this was not always so (compare 10:32-34). The same adjective comes back in 6:12, so 5:11-6:12 is framed by it: here they are dull listeners, there the author hopes they will not become sluggish in hope.

decisions.choice: sluggish (Balanced), lazy (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same English word is used here and in 6:12 at each level, so the reader can see the frame the author builds.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms (for the chapter)
decisions.reason: The author addresses his readers in the plural. As elsewhere in the Spanish New Testament, every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

decisions.choice: tardos (L), lentos (B), perezosos (R)
decisions.reason: The same Spanish word is used here and in 6:12 at each level, as in English, so the reader can see the frame the author builds (see the meaning decision). Readable "perezosos" matches the English Readable "lazy".

decisions.choice: wazito (L, B), wavivu (R)
decisions.reason: The same Swahili words are used here and in 6:12, as the English and the meaning decision there link the two. "Mzito" (heavy, slow) is dullness of mind; Readable "wavivu" matches the English Readable "lazy".

decisions.choice: vous for the readers, no setting (for the book)
decisions.reason: The readers are a group, so French uses the plural "vous" as every modern French Bible does; unlike Spanish there is no regional variant, so no setting is needed. "Tu" is kept for one person and for God speaking to the Son.

decisions.choice: lents d’oreille (L), lents à écouter (B), paresseux pour écouter (R)
decisions.reason: "Durs d’oreille" means hard of hearing, which is not the point; the word is about being slow and dull in taking in teaching. The same word returns in 6:12, rendered "lents" (L, B) and "paresseux" (R) there too.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" for the writer speaking of himself and his teaching (also 6:9-11; 13:18)
decisions.reason: Here "we" is the writer, set against "you" the readers (m2), so Vietnamese uses the exclusive "chúng tôi", where elsewhere the inclusive "chúng ta" takes the readers in.

decisions.choice: lentos (L, B); preguiçosos (R)
decisions.reason: The same adjective returns in 6:12 and frames 5:11-6:12 (m3), so each level uses one word in both places: "lentos" at Literal and Balanced (6:12 "não se tornem lentos"), "preguiçosos" at Readable, as the English keeps "sluggish" and "lazy".

decisions.choice: "सुस्त" (L, B); "आलसी" (R)
decisions.reason: The same Hindi word is used here and in 6:12 at each level, so the reader can see the frame the author builds (as the English rendering decision says).

source.text: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς τινὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Even for owing to be teachers because of the time, again need you have [of] the [one] to teach you someone the elements of the beginning of the oracles of the God, and you have become need having of milk, not of solid food.

en.L: For indeed, though you ought to be teachers by reason of the time, again you have need of someone to teach you the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have become [people] having need of milk, not of solid food.
en.B: Given the time that has passed, you ought to be teachers by now; yet once more you need someone to teach you the most basic elements of God's oracles. You have become people who need milk rather than solid food.
en.R: You have had enough time that you should be teaching others by now. But you need someone to teach you the ABCs of God's message all over again. You have become people who need milk, not solid food.

es.L: Porque, en efecto, debiendo ser maestros por razón del tiempo, otra vez {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} necesidad de que alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñe los elementos del principio de los oráculos de Dios, y {{plural_you:han llegado|habéis llegado}} a ser [personas] que tienen necesidad de leche, no de alimento sólido.
es.B: Por el tiempo que ha pasado, ya {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} ser maestros; y sin embargo otra vez {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} que alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñe los elementos más básicos de los oráculos de Dios. {{plural_you:Han llegado|Habéis llegado}} a ser personas que necesitan leche y no alimento sólido.
es.R: Ya ha pasado bastante tiempo; a estas alturas {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} estar enseñando a otros. Pero {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} que alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} vuelva a enseñar el abecé del mensaje de Dios. {{plural_you:Se han vuelto|Os habéis vuelto}} personas que necesitan leche, no alimento sólido.

fr.L: Car en effet, alors que vous devriez être des enseignants en raison du temps, vous avez de nouveau besoin que quelqu’un vous enseigne les éléments du commencement des oracles de Dieu, et vous êtes devenus [des gens] ayant besoin de lait, non de nourriture solide.
fr.B: Vu le temps écoulé, vous devriez être des enseignants à présent ; et pourtant il faut encore qu’on vous enseigne les tout premiers éléments des oracles de Dieu. Vous êtes devenus des gens qui ont besoin de lait plutôt que de nourriture solide.
fr.R: Depuis le temps, vous devriez déjà enseigner les autres. Mais il faut que quelqu’un vous réapprenne l’abc du message de Dieu. Vous êtes devenus des gens qui ont besoin de lait, et non de nourriture solide.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa kweli, ingawa mnapaswa kuwa walimu kwa sababu ya muda, tena mnahitaji mtu wa kuwafundisha mambo ya msingi ya mwanzo wa kauli za Mungu, na mmekuwa [watu] wenye haja ya maziwa, wala si ya chakula kigumu.
sw.B: Kwa muda uliopita, mngepaswa kuwa walimu sasa; lakini bado mnahitaji tena mtu wa kuwafundisha mambo ya msingi kabisa ya kauli za Mungu. Mmekuwa watu wenye haja ya maziwa badala ya chakula kigumu.
sw.R: Mmekuwa na muda wa kutosha hata mngepaswa kuwa mnawafundisha wengine sasa. Lakini mnahitaji mtu wa kuwafundisha tena A, B, C za ujumbe wa Mungu. Mmekuwa watu wa kunywa maziwa tu, si wa kula chakula kigumu.

vi.L: Vì đáng lẽ theo thời gian anh chị em đã phải là thầy dạy, thế mà anh chị em lại cần có người dạy cho mình những điều sơ đẳng của các lời phán của Đức Chúa Trời, và anh chị em đã trở nên những người cần sữa, chứ không phải thức ăn đặc.
vi.B: Theo thời gian đã qua, đáng lẽ bây giờ anh chị em đã phải làm thầy dạy người khác; vậy mà anh chị em lại cần có người dạy lại cho mình những điều sơ đẳng nhất trong các lời phán của Đức Chúa Trời. Anh chị em đã trở nên những người cần sữa thay vì thức ăn đặc.
vi.R: Anh chị em đã có đủ thời gian để bây giờ có thể dạy người khác. Nhưng anh chị em lại cần có người dạy lại cho mình những bài học vỡ lòng về sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời. Anh chị em đã trở nên những người cần uống sữa, chứ không ăn được thức ăn đặc.

ko.L: 시간으로 보면 여러분은 마땅히 선생이 되어야 할 터인데, 다시 누군가가 여러분에게 하나님의 말씀의 첫 원리들을 가르쳐 줄 필요가 있습니다. 여러분은 단단한 음식이 아니라 젖이 필요한 사람들이 되었습니다.
ko.B: 지금쯤이면 여러분은 이미 선생이 되었어야 합니다. 그런데 여러분에게는 하나님 말씀의 가장 기초적인 원리를 다시 가르쳐 줄 사람이 필요합니다. 여러분은 단단한 음식이 아니라 젖을 먹어야 하는 사람들이 되었습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 이미 충분한 시간을 보냈으니, 지금쯤은 다른 사람들을 가르치고 있어야 합니다. 그런데 누군가가 하나님 말씀의 가장 쉬운 기초를 처음부터 다시 가르쳐 주어야 할 형편입니다. 여러분은 단단한 음식이 아니라 젖을 먹어야 하는 사람들이 되었습니다.

pt.L: Pois, de fato, devendo vocês ser mestres por causa do tempo, de novo precisam de alguém que lhes ensine os elementos do princípio dos oráculos de Deus, e vocês se tornaram [pessoas] que precisam de leite, não de alimento sólido.
pt.B: Considerando o tempo que já passou, vocês já deveriam ser mestres; no entanto, ainda precisam de alguém que lhes ensine outra vez os elementos mais básicos dos oráculos de Deus. Vocês se tornaram pessoas que precisam de leite, e não de alimento sólido.
pt.R: Vocês já tiveram tempo suficiente para estar ensinando outras pessoas. Mas precisam de alguém que ensine a vocês de novo o bê-á-bá da mensagem de Deus. Vocês se tornaram pessoas que precisam de leite, não de comida sólida.

am.L: ከጊዜው የተነሣ አስተማሪዎች ልትሆኑ ሲገባችሁ፣ የእግዚአብሔርን ቃሎች የመጀመሪያ መሠረታውያን ማንም እንዲያስተምራችሁ እንደ ገና ያስፈልጋችኋልና፤ ጠንካራ ምግብ ሳይሆን ወተት የሚያስፈልጋችሁ ሆናችኋል።
am.B: ካለፈው ጊዜ አንጻር እስከ አሁን አስተማሪዎች ልትሆኑ ይገባችሁ ነበር፤ ነገር ግን የእግዚአብሔርን ቃል መሠረታዊ ትምህርቶች የሚያስተምራችሁ ሰው እንደ ገና ያስፈልጋችኋል። ጠንካራ ምግብ ሳይሆን ወተት የሚያስፈልጋችሁ ሰዎች ሆናችኋል።
am.R: ሌሎችን አሁን ማስተማር የምትችሉበት በቂ ጊዜ ነበራችሁ። እናንተ ግን የእግዚአብሔርን መልእክት ሀ ሁ የሚያስተምራችሁ ሰው እንደ ገና ያስፈልጋችኋል። ጠንካራ ምግብ ሳይሆን ወተት የሚያስፈልጋችሁ ሰዎች ሆናችኋል።

hi.L: क्योंकि समय के हिसाब से तुम्हें शिक्षक हो जाना चाहिए था, फिर भी तुम्हें इसकी आवश्यकता है कि कोई तुम्हें परमेश्वर के वचनों की आरंभ की प्राथमिक बातें फिर से सिखाए, और तुम ऐसे हो गए हो जिन्हें दूध की आवश्यकता है, ठोस भोजन की नहीं।
hi.B: इतना समय बीत चुका है कि अब तक तुम्हें शिक्षक बन जाना चाहिए था; फिर भी तुम्हें इसकी ज़रूरत है कि कोई तुम्हें परमेश्वर के वचनों की सबसे पहली बुनियादी बातें फिर से सिखाए। तुम ऐसे लोग बन गए हो जिन्हें ठोस भोजन नहीं, दूध चाहिए।
hi.R: तुम्हें इतना समय मिल चुका है कि अब तक तुम्हें दूसरों को सिखाना चाहिए था। पर तुम्हें ज़रूरत है कि कोई तुम्हें परमेश्वर के संदेश की वर्णमाला फिर से सिखाए। तुम ऐसे लोग बन गए हो जिन्हें दूध चाहिए, ठोस भोजन नहीं।

ru.L: Ведь, хотя по времени вы должны быть учителями, вы снова нуждаетесь в том, чтобы кто-то учил вас начальным основам Божьих изречений, и вы стали нуждающимися в молоке, а не в твёрдой пище.
ru.B: Судя по времени, вы уже должны быть учителями; но вам снова нужно, чтобы кто-то учил вас самым начальным основам Божьих изречений. Вы стали людьми, которым нужно молоко, а не твёрдая пища.
ru.R: У вас было достаточно времени, чтобы самим уже учить других. Но вам нужно, чтобы кто-то снова учил вас азбуке Божьей вести. Вы стали людьми, которым нужно молоко, а не твёрдая пища.

uk.L: Бо хоч ви з огляду на час мали б бути вчителями, вам знову потрібно, щоб хтось навчав вас перших основ Божих слів, і ви стали [такими], що потребують молока, а не твердої їжі.
uk.B: Зважаючи на те, скільки часу минуло, ви вже мали б бути вчителями; а вам знову потрібно, щоб хтось навчав вас найпростіших основ Божих слів. Ви стали тими, кому потрібне молоко, а не тверда їжа.
uk.R: У вас було досить часу, щоб тепер уже навчати інших. Але вам знову потрібно, щоб хтось учив вас азбуки Божої звістки. Ви стали людьми, яким потрібне молоко, а не тверда їжа.

ja.L: 実に、あなたがたは、時間からすれば教師であるべきなのに、再び、神の言葉の初歩の基本をだれかに教えてもらう必要があります。そして、固い食物ではなく、乳を必要とする者になってしまっています。
ja.B: あなたがたは、これだけの時がたったのですから、もう教える者になっているはずです。それなのに、神の言葉のいちばん初歩的なことを、もう一度だれかに教えてもらう必要があります。あなたがたは、固い食べ物ではなく、乳を必要とする者になってしまいました。
ja.R: みなさんは、もう十分に時間がたったのですから、今ではほかの人たちを教えていてもよいはずです。それなのに、神の言葉のいちばん初めのことを、もう一度だれかに教えてもらう必要があります。みなさんは、固い食べ物ではなく、まだ乳を飲まなければならない人のようになっています。

decisions.choice: someone: you need someone to teach you
alternatives: what: you need to be taught what the elements are
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have no accents. The SBLGNT accents the word as τινὰ, the indefinite "someone", the subject of "to teach". Accented the other way it would be the question word "what", giving "you need someone to teach you what the elements are". The sense is nearly the same.

decisions.choice: the first elements of God's oracles: the most basic teaching of what God has spoken
alternatives: the first letters of the alphabet
decisions.reason: στοιχεῖα are the elements of a thing, such as the letters of the alphabet or the first principles of a subject; "of the beginning" makes the point stronger. "The oracles of God" are God's spoken words, the Scriptures (Romans 3:2; Acts 7:38), and here also the message about Christ built on them.

decisions.choice: milk and solid food: elementary teaching and mature teaching
decisions.reason: Milk is food for infants; solid food is for adults. The author uses the picture for the first teachings (listed in 6:1-2) and for fuller teaching, here the priesthood of Christ like Melchizedek's. Paul uses the same picture in 1 Corinthians 3:1-2. In 1 Peter 2:2 milk is a good picture for the word itself; the point here is not that milk is bad but that the readers should have outgrown living on it.

decisions.choice: the ABCs of God's message
alternatives: the basic principles of God's word
decisions.reason: "ABCs" gives the picture behind στοιχεῖα (the letters one learns first) in everyday words.

decisions.choice: kauli za Mungu (L, B), ujumbe wa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means utterances spoken by God. "Kauli" is a spoken statement; "neno la Mungu" would be taken as the Bible as a whole, and "maneno ya Mungu" is the familiar wording of other versions.

decisions.choice: A, B, C za ujumbe wa Mungu
decisions.reason: Follows the English Readable picture of the first letters. "Alifu, be, te" is the older Swahili idiom for the first letters and may sound more natural to some readers; a native reviewer should choose.

decisions.choice: "những điều sơ đẳng của các lời phán của Đức Chúa Trời" (L, B); "những bài học vỡ lòng về sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: The oracles are what God has spoken (m2); "lời phán" is the word for God's speaking. Readable's "bài học vỡ lòng" is the Vietnamese picture for a beginner's first lessons, where the English Readable says "the ABCs".

decisions.choice: o bê-á-bá
decisions.reason: "Bê-á-bá" is the everyday Brazilian word for the first letters a child learns, the picture behind the Greek word (m2), as the English Readable says "ABCs".

decisions.choice: ሀ ሁ (the ABCs)
decisions.reason: Amharic names the first letters of its syllabary, ሀ ሁ, as English names the ABCs, so Readable can use the same everyday picture for the most basic teaching.

decisions.choice: "वर्णमाला" (R); "प्राथमिक बातें" (L); "बुनियादी बातें" (B)
decisions.reason: The word pictures the letters one learns first (meaning decision m2); Readable uses the picture of the alphabet, as the English says "ABCs".

decisions.choice: азбуке
decisions.reason: As the English Readable says "the ABCs", Russian Readable says "азбука", the everyday picture of the first things one learns.

decisions.choice: "Божі слова"
decisions.reason: The word means utterances, what God has spoken (m2); "слова" says that plainly. Readable has "Божа звістка" and "азбука" for the English "ABCs".

decisions.choice: "神の言葉の初歩の基本" (L), "神の言葉のいちばん初歩的なこと" (B), "いちばん初めのこと" (R)
decisions.reason: The "elements of the beginning of the oracles of God" are the most basic teaching of what God has spoken; Japanese "初歩" covers the English Readable's ABCs without a foreign image.

source.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης, νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: Everyone for the [one] partaking of milk [is] inexperienced in word of righteousness, an infant for he is.

en.L: For everyone who partakes of milk [is] inexperienced in [the] word of righteousness, for [such a one] is an infant.
en.B: Whoever feeds on milk has no experience in the word of righteousness; that person is still an infant.
en.R: Anyone who is still drinking milk is a baby and has no experience with the teaching about righteousness.

es.L: Porque todo el que se alimenta de leche [es] inexperto en [la] palabra de justicia, porque es un niño pequeño.
es.B: Quien se alimenta de leche no tiene experiencia en la palabra de justicia; esa persona es todavía un niño pequeño.
es.R: Quien todavía toma leche es un bebé y no tiene experiencia con la enseñanza sobre la justicia.

fr.L: Car quiconque prend du lait [est] sans expérience de [la] parole de justice, car il est un petit enfant.
fr.B: Celui qui se nourrit de lait n’a aucune expérience de la parole de justice ; il est encore un petit enfant.
fr.R: Celui qui boit encore du lait est un bébé, et il n’a pas d’expérience de l’enseignement sur ce qui est juste.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila ashirikiye maziwa [ni] mgeni katika neno la haki, kwa maana [huyo] ni mtoto mchanga.
sw.B: Anayelishwa maziwa hana uzoefu katika neno la haki; mtu huyo bado ni mtoto mchanga.
sw.R: Mtu ambaye bado anakunywa maziwa ni mtoto mchanga, naye hana uzoefu na mafundisho kuhusu haki.

vi.L: Vì ai còn dùng sữa thì không có kinh nghiệm về lời của sự công chính, vì người ấy là trẻ thơ.
vi.B: Ai còn bú sữa thì chưa có kinh nghiệm về lời dạy của sự công chính; người ấy vẫn còn là trẻ thơ.
vi.R: Ai còn uống sữa thì vẫn còn là em bé, và chưa có kinh nghiệm về lời dạy về sự công chính.

ko.L: 젖을 먹는 사람은 누구나 의의 말씀에 익숙하지 못합니다. 그는 어린아이이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 젖을 먹고 사는 사람은 누구나 의의 말씀을 경험해 보지 못한 사람입니다. 그는 아직 어린아이입니다.
ko.R: 아직 젖을 먹는 사람은 아기입니다. 그런 사람은 의에 대한 가르침을 경험해 보지 못했습니다.

pt.L: Pois todo aquele que se alimenta de leite [é] inexperiente na palavra da justiça, pois é criancinha.
pt.B: Quem se alimenta de leite não tem experiência na palavra da justiça; essa pessoa ainda é uma criancinha.
pt.R: Quem ainda está tomando leite é um bebê e não tem experiência com o ensino sobre a justiça.

am.L: ወተት የሚካፈል ሁሉ በጽድቅ ቃል ልምድ የሌለው ነውና፤ ሕፃን ነውና።
am.B: ወተት የሚመገብ ሁሉ በጽድቅ ቃል ልምድ የለውም፤ ገና ሕፃን ነው።
am.R: ገና ወተት የሚጠጣ ሰው ሕፃን ነው፤ ስለ ጽድቅ በሚናገረው ትምህርትም ልምድ የለውም።

hi.L: क्योंकि दूध पीनेवाला हर कोई धार्मिकता के वचन से अनजान [है], क्योंकि वह बच्चा है;
hi.B: जो दूध पर ही पलता है, उसे धार्मिकता के वचन का कोई अनुभव नहीं; वह अभी बच्चा ही है।
hi.R: जो अभी भी दूध पीता है, वह छोटा बच्चा है, और उसे धार्मिकता की शिक्षा का कोई अनुभव नहीं है।

ru.L: Ведь всякий питающийся молоком несведущ в слове праведности, ведь он младенец.
ru.B: Кто питается молоком, тот не имеет опыта в слове праведности: он ещё младенец.
ru.R: Кто всё ещё пьёт молоко, тот — младенец. У него нет опыта в учении о праведности.

uk.L: Бо кожен, хто живиться молоком, недосвідчений у слові праведності, бо він немовля.
uk.B: Хто живиться молоком, той не має досвіду в слові праведності: він ще немовля.
uk.R: Хто ще пʼє молоко, той — немовля, і він не має досвіду в навчанні про праведність.

ja.L: というのは、乳を飲んでいる者はみな、義の言葉に未熟だからです。その人は幼子なのです。
ja.B: 乳を飲んでいる者はだれでも、義の言葉に慣れていません。その人はまだ幼子なのです。
ja.R: まだ乳を飲んでいる人は、赤ちゃんです。正しいことについての教えを、まだ経験していません。

decisions.choice: the word of righteousness: teaching about righteousness, the kind that trains a person to tell right from wrong
alternatives: ordinary adult speech, which an infant cannot follow
the message that God makes people righteous
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It can mean the message about righteousness, mature teaching that shapes a person in what is right, which suits verse 14 (training to tell good from evil). Since "infant" can mean one who cannot yet speak, some take it as normal, correct speech. Others hear the message of how God makes people righteous. The translation keeps "word of righteousness" so all of these remain open.

decisions.choice: infant: a young child, the opposite of the mature in verse 14
decisions.reason: νήπιος is a little child. Deuteronomy 1:39 describes little children as those who do not yet know good from evil, the very thing the mature can do in verse 14.

decisions.choice: has no experience
decisions.reason: ἄπειρος means without experience or trial of something; "has no experience" says it simply and fits the picture of a child who has not yet learned.

decisions.choice: parole de justice (L, B), l’enseignement sur ce qui est juste (R)
decisions.reason: "Justice" is the usual French for this word in the Bible, though in everyday French it suggests courts. The Readable says "ce qui est juste", the right as against the wrong, which is what the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "義の言葉" (L, B), "正しいことについての教え" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as teaching about righteousness that trains a person to tell right from wrong (uncertain); Balanced keeps the Greek phrase open.

source.text: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή, τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Of perfect [ones] but is the solid food, of the [ones] through the practice the faculties trained having for distinguishing good both and evil.

en.L: But solid food is for [the] perfect, for those who through practice have [their] faculties trained for distinguishing both good and evil.
en.B: Solid food, on the other hand, belongs to the mature, whose faculties have been trained by practice to tell good from evil.
en.R: But solid food is for grown-ups. They have used their powers of judgment again and again and trained them to tell what is good from what is evil.

es.L: Pero el alimento sólido es para [los] perfectos, los que por la práctica tienen [sus] facultades entrenadas para distinguir tanto el bien como el mal.
es.B: El alimento sólido, en cambio, es para los maduros, que por la práctica tienen sus facultades entrenadas para distinguir el bien del mal.
es.R: Pero el alimento sólido es para los que ya han madurado. Ellos han usado una y otra vez su capacidad de juzgar, y la han entrenado para distinguir lo bueno de lo malo.

fr.L: Mais la nourriture solide est pour [les] parfaits, pour ceux qui, par la pratique, ont [leurs] facultés exercées à discerner le bien et le mal.
fr.B: La nourriture solide, elle, est pour les adultes, dont les facultés ont été exercées par la pratique à distinguer le bien du mal.
fr.R: Mais la nourriture solide est pour les adultes. Ils ont utilisé leur jugement encore et encore, et l’ont entraîné à distinguer ce qui est bien de ce qui est mal.

sw.L: Lakini chakula kigumu ni cha [watu] wakamilifu, wale ambao kwa sababu ya mazoea wana milango ya fahamu iliyofunzwa kwa kutofautisha jema na baya.
sw.B: Chakula kigumu, kwa upande mwingine, ni cha watu wakomavu, ambao uwezo wao wa kutambua umefunzwa kwa mazoezi ili kutofautisha jema na baya.
sw.R: Lakini chakula kigumu ni cha watu wakomavu, yaani watu wazima. Wametumia uwezo wao wa kupima mambo tena na tena, na wameuzoeza kutofautisha lililo jema na lililo baya.

vi.L: Nhưng thức ăn đặc là cho những người trưởng thành, là những người nhờ luyện tập mà các giác quan đã được rèn luyện để phân biệt điều thiện và điều ác.
vi.B: Còn thức ăn đặc là dành cho người trưởng thành, là những người nhờ thực hành mà khả năng nhận biết đã được rèn luyện để phân biệt điều thiện với điều ác.
vi.R: Nhưng thức ăn đặc là cho người lớn. Họ đã dùng khả năng phán đoán của mình nhiều lần và đã rèn luyện nó để biết đâu là điều tốt, đâu là điều ác.

ko.L: 그러나 단단한 음식은 완전한 사람들, 곧 꾸준한 연습으로 선과 악을 분별하도록 감각이 훈련된 사람들의 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 단단한 음식은 장성한 사람들의 것입니다. 그들은 꾸준히 연습하여 선과 악을 분별하도록 감각을 훈련한 사람들입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 단단한 음식은 어른들을 위한 것입니다. 어른들은 판단하는 힘을 거듭 사용하여, 무엇이 선하고 무엇이 악한지 가려내도록 훈련했습니다.

pt.L: Mas o alimento sólido é para os perfeitos, para os que pela prática têm as [suas] faculdades exercitadas para distinguir tanto o bem quanto o mal.
pt.B: O alimento sólido, por outro lado, é para os maduros, que pela prática têm as faculdades treinadas para distinguir o bem do mal.
pt.R: Mas a comida sólida é para os adultos. Eles usaram a sua capacidade de julgar muitas e muitas vezes e a treinaram para distinguir o que é bom do que é mau.

am.L: ጠንካራ ምግብ ግን ለፍጹማን ነው፤ ይኸውም በልምምድ ምክንያት መልካሙንና ክፉውን ለመለየት የሰለጠኑ የማስተዋል ችሎታዎች ላሏቸው ነው።
am.B: ጠንካራ ምግብ ግን ለበሰሉት ነው፤ እነርሱም መልካሙን ከክፉው ለመለየት የማስተዋል ችሎታቸው በልምምድ የሰለጠነ ነው።
am.R: ጠንካራ ምግብ ግን ለአዋቂዎች ነው። እነርሱ የማመዛዘን ችሎታቸውን ደጋግመው ተጠቅመዋል፤ መልካሙን ከክፉው እንዲለዩም አሰልጥነውታል።

hi.L: पर ठोस भोजन सिद्ध [लोगों] के लिए है, जिनकी ज्ञानेंद्रियाँ अभ्यास के कारण भले और बुरे में भेद करने के लिए पक्की हो गई हैं।
hi.B: पर ठोस भोजन परिपक्व लोगों के लिए है, जिनकी समझ अभ्यास से इतनी प्रशिक्षित हो गई है कि वे भले और बुरे में भेद कर सकें।
hi.R: पर ठोस भोजन बड़ों के लिए है। उन्होंने बार-बार अपनी परखने की शक्ति का उपयोग करके उसे इतना साध लिया है कि वे पहचान सकें कि क्या भला है और क्या बुरा।

ru.L: Твёрдая же пища — для совершенных, у которых благодаря навыку чувства приучены к различению и добра, и зла.
ru.B: А твёрдая пища — для зрелых, у которых способность суждения навыком приучена отличать добро от зла.
ru.R: А твёрдая пища — для взрослых. Они снова и снова упражняли свою способность судить и научились отличать хорошее от плохого.

uk.L: А тверда їжа — для досконалих, для тих, хто через вправляння має чуття, натреновані розрізняти і добро, і зло.
uk.B: А тверда їжа — для зрілих, чиї чуття вправою натреновані відрізняти добро від зла.
uk.R: А тверда їжа — для дорослих. Вони знову й знову вправляли свою здатність судити і навчилися відрізняти добре від злого.

ja.L: しかし、固い食物は、成熟した者たちのもの、すなわち、習慣によって感覚を訓練され、善と悪を見分けられる者たちのものです。
ja.B: これに対して、固い食べ物は、成熟した大人のものです。彼らは、使い慣れることによって感覚が訓練され、善と悪を見分けることができます。
ja.R: しかし、固い食べ物は大人のためのものです。大人は、何度も何度も自分の判断する力を使って、それを訓練してきました。ですから、何が良いことで、何が悪いことかを見分けることができるのです。

decisions.choice: perfect: mature, fully grown, as opposed to infants
decisions.reason: τελείων is from the same family as "made perfect" in 5:9 and "perfection" in 6:1. Set against "infant" in verse 13, it means a grown adult. The author chooses the word to link the readers' growth with the goal Christ has reached (5:9).

decisions.choice: faculties trained by practice: powers of perception exercised until they work by habit
decisions.reason: αἰσθητήρια are the senses or powers of perception. γεγυμνασμένα is the verb of athletic training (from it comes "gymnasium"); 12:11 uses it again for training by discipline. ἕξιν is a settled state reached by practice.

decisions.choice: to tell good from evil: moral discernment, the mark of an adult
alternatives: to tell good food from bad
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament, knowing good and evil marks the move from childhood to maturity (Deuteronomy 1:39; Isaiah 7:15-16). The food picture continues, but the point is the ability to judge what is right.

decisions.choice: mature (Balanced), grown-ups (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "perfect" to show the link with 5:9 and 6:1. Balanced and Readable say "mature" and "grown-ups", because "perfect" set against "infant" would mislead.

decisions.choice: perfectos (L), maduros (B), los que ya han madurado (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "perfectos" for the link with 5:9 and 6:1. Balanced and Readable use the "maduro" family, as in 6:1 ("madurez", "maduremos"), so the Spanish keeps the link between the two verses that the English "mature" and "grow up" give. "Adultos" would fit the food picture but loses that link.

decisions.choice: wakamilifu (L), wakomavu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word family of "kukamilisha" (make perfect) that Hebrews uses throughout; Balanced and Readable say "wakomavu" (mature), as the English says "mature", and the same pair returns in 6:1 ("ukamilifu", "ukomavu"). Readable adds "watu wazima" for the English "grown-ups".

decisions.choice: milango ya fahamu
decisions.reason: The Greek word means the organs of perception; "milango ya fahamu" is the Swahili term for the senses, used here of moral perception as the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: parfaits (L), adultes (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as "mature, fully grown", in contrast with the infant of verse 13. Literal keeps the link with "perfect" elsewhere in Hebrews; Balanced and Readable say "adultes", the plain opposite of a little child (and "maturité" in 6:1). "Hommes faits" would exclude women.

decisions.choice: "người trưởng thành" (L, B); "người lớn" (R) for "the perfect"
decisions.reason: Here the word means mature, fully grown, set against infants (m1), so Vietnamese says "trưởng thành", as the Vietnamese Philippians does (3:15), and keeps "trọn vẹn" for "made perfect" (2:10; 5:9), where the sense is brought to the goal.

decisions.choice: "완전한 사람들" (L); "장성한 사람들" (B); "어른들" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means mature, fully grown, as against infants (meaning decision). Literal keeps "완전" so the link with "완전하게 하다" (2:10; 5:9) can be traced; Balanced and Readable say grown-up, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ፍጹማን (the perfect) at Literal; የበሰሉ (the mature, B), አዋቂዎች (grown-ups, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for perfect that runs through Hebrews (2:10; 5:9), so the link with Christ being made perfect shows; Balanced and Readable give the sense here, mature as opposed to infants.
Literal keeps "सिद्ध" to show the link with 5:9 and 6:1; Balanced and Readable say "mature" and "grown-ups", as the English does, because "सिद्ध" set against a child would mislead.

decisions.choice: "成熟した者" (L), "成熟した大人" (B), "大人" (R) for teleioi
decisions.reason: Here the word means mature, grown up, in contrast to infants; Japanese uses the word for maturity, not "完全", which the book keeps for teleioo of Christ.
